p2/esc1091:0.speaker: seeker
p2/esc1091:0.text: Hello. I wanted to talk about my academic pressures.

p2/esc1091:1.speaker: supporter
p2/esc1091:1.text: Hi there. What academic pressures are troubling you today?

p2/esc1091:10.speaker: seeker
p2/esc1091:10.text: What should I do to relax my mind?

p2/esc1091:11.speaker: supporter
p2/esc1091:11.text: Have you thought about seeking advice from a close friend or family member?

p2/esc1091:12.speaker: seeker
p2/esc1091:12.text: Not yet, I am scared to tell my family, considering that they view academic success heavily

p2/esc1091:13.speaker: seeker
p2/esc1091:13.text: With friends, most are busy with their own struggles and I don't want to be bothering them as much

p2/esc1091:14.speaker: supporter
p2/esc1091:14.text: I see, it sounds like you are dealing with your academic pressures all on your own right now then?

p2/esc1091:15.speaker: seeker
p2/esc1091:15.text: Totally. Feels pretty tiring and heavy

p2/esc1091:16.speaker: supporter
p2/esc1091:16.text: Is there possibly a school councilor you could seek advice from?

p2/esc1091:17.speaker: seeker
p2/esc1091:17.text: Maybe, but it feels scary and very awkward to seek them

p2/esc1091:18.speaker: supporter
p2/esc1091:18.text: I hear you, it's definitely not for everyone.

p2/esc1091:19.speaker: seeker
p2/esc1091:19.text: thank you for understanding and talking with me

p2/esc1091:2.speaker: seeker
p2/esc1091:2.text: Just lots of classes and expectations. Especially with group projects.

p2/esc1091:20.speaker: supporter
p2/esc1091:20.text: Of course! We all need an ear to listen once in a while :)

p2/esc1091:21.speaker: seeker
p2/esc1091:21.text: It really helps to get this off my chest

p2/esc1091:22.speaker: supporter
p2/esc1091:22.text: I'm so happy to hear that, it sounds like this was something building up. It's always good to let things out in one way or another.

p2/esc1091:24.speaker: supporter
p2/esc1091:24.text: Is there anything else you would like to talk about today?

p2/esc1091:27.speaker: supporter
p2/esc1091:27.text: Okay, and of course! I'm glad I could help.

p2/esc1091:3.speaker: seeker
p2/esc1091:3.text: Needed someone to talk to about my stress and workload. I don't know what to do with these horrible group members.

p2/esc1091:4.speaker: supporter
p2/esc1091:4.text: I see. It sounds like being in the group project is especially stressing you out. Would you say that's pretty true?

p2/esc1091:5.speaker: seeker
p2/esc1091:5.text: Yes. I have roughly 3 different classes all requiring a group project.

p2/esc1091:6.speaker: supporter
p2/esc1091:6.text: I totally understand. When I was in school I remember being stressed out when we had mandatory group projects as well. Having to deal with others can be a bit stressful at times.

p2/esc1091:7.speaker: seeker
p2/esc1091:7.text: I agree. I also just don't know which project to proritize

p2/esc1091:8.speaker: supporter
p2/esc1091:8.text: I hear you, it sounds like you have a lot going on.

p2/esc150:0.speaker: supporter
p2/esc150:0.text: hi there! how are you feeling today?

p2/esc150:10.speaker: supporter
p2/esc150:10.text: It sounds like writing your feelings down helped you greatly in the past. May I suggest going back to writing and even letting someone you trust read what you have written down to understand how you are feeling?

p2/esc150:11.speaker: seeker
p2/esc150:11.text: yes, writing has been a huge help for me. I would take your suggestion and begin writing again to feel better. and i have let others read what i wrote and they have said it has helped them get over their depression and helped them understand me more

p2/esc150:12.speaker: supporter
p2/esc150:12.text: That's great! I am glad to hear that you will begin writing again. Thank you for opening up to me about your feelings. How do you feel about the solution we have come to today?

p2/esc150:13.speaker: seeker
p2/esc150:13.text: now that i was able to talk about how i feel with you and you giving me a useful suggestion i feel less depressed and feel motivated to write again. your help has been really helpful for me

p2/esc150:14.speaker: supporter
p2/esc150:14.text: That's wonderful! I appreciate your honesty about how you are feeling. I am proud of you for seeking help. Is there anything else you would like to discuss?

p2/esc150:15.speaker: seeker
p2/esc150:15.text: thank you so much for helping me. and that is all that i would like to discuss. you have been a big help for me

p2/esc150:16.speaker: supporter
p2/esc150:16.text: I am glad I could be here for you! I am hoping you continue to feel better and your writing helps to work out these feelings.  Thank you so much for being open with me. I hope you have a fantastic rest of your day! :)

p2/esc150:17.speaker: seeker
p2/esc150:17.text: thank you. hope you enjoy your day

p2/esc150:2.speaker: supporter
p2/esc150:2.text: i'm sorry to hear that. is there a specific reason you are having these feelings?

p2/esc150:3.speaker: seeker
p2/esc150:3.text: i feel alone. i feel like i do not have anyone to talk to when it comes to my emotions.

p2/esc150:4.speaker: supporter
p2/esc150:4.text: I understand. I have been feeling quite lonely too, I find myself feeling lonely at work and struggling to find someone I trust to talk to about these emotions. Do you have a friend or family member that you trust who might understand some of these feelings?

p2/esc150:5.speaker: seeker
p2/esc150:5.text: i do have a few friends that i think i can talk to about how i am feeling however the thought of them being too busy with their work is what prevents me from reaching out to them.

p2/esc150:6.speaker: supporter
p2/esc150:6.text: I understand. Correct me if i'm wrong, it sounds like you're nervous to open up to these trusted people because you think they might be distracted by their work to provide the empathy you need and fully understand how you are feeling. Does that sound right?

p2/esc150:7.speaker: seeker
p2/esc150:7.text: you know i think that you are right about this. it has always been difficult for me to open to others even with those that have been there for me when i needed someone. i feel like a mix of emotions nervous but at the same time wanting to reaching out for help

p2/esc150:8.speaker: supporter
p2/esc150:8.text: I understand these feelings very well. Sometimes, my fear overshadows my want for help. I find it easier to open up to others through writing rather than face to face. Have you considered putting your feelings in writing and opening up to trusted friends and family in this way?

p2/esc150:9.speaker: seeker
p2/esc150:9.text: i have been writing for a while but due to my emotions i have stopped writing like i used to. when i did write i did notice a change in my feelings it became more positive and less depressed. now that i stopped writing its like i went back into depression

p2/esc611:1.speaker: seeker
p2/esc611:1.text: hi. my friend told my ex boyfriend he was an idiot for dumping me. it made me feel uncomfortable since i was in the same room. now he is talking to me again. i think he might want me back

p2/esc611:10.speaker: supporter
p2/esc611:10.text: Do you feel his change is genuine?

p2/esc611:11.speaker: seeker
p2/esc611:11.text: to a degree. i think he has ulterior motives too.

p2/esc611:12.speaker: supporter
p2/esc611:12.text: What would he have to do to prove himself?

p2/esc611:13.speaker: seeker
p2/esc611:13.text: say he wants me back or something to that effect. i'd like him to be more direct in what he wants from me

p2/esc611:14.speaker: supporter
p2/esc611:14.text: It sounds like it would help if he were direct with you and not sending mixed signals.  Is that correct?

p2/esc611:15.speaker: seeker
p2/esc611:15.text: yes that would be nice. he tends to beat around the bush then lets me know

p2/esc611:16.speaker: supporter
p2/esc611:16.text: Have you talked to anyone else besides your friend about your concerns?  Do you think your family or other friends could give some additional support to you?

p2/esc611:17.speaker: seeker
p2/esc611:17.text: yes i've talked to them about it. they've given me some insight into it. i know they want me to be careful. they don't want me to be hurt

p2/esc611:18.speaker: supporter
p2/esc611:18.text: That's understandable that they want you to be careful.  My parents and friends watched out for me too.

p2/esc611:19.speaker: seeker
p2/esc611:19.text: we are lucky they look out for us. they can't all be wrong if they're guiding us a certain way

p2/esc611:2.speaker: supporter
p2/esc611:2.text: What are your thoughts on the relationship?

p2/esc611:20.speaker: supporter
p2/esc611:20.text: I think you hit the nail on the head that it's helpful to have that support.

p2/esc611:21.speaker: seeker
p2/esc611:21.text: absolutely. i appreciate your help! nity nite

p2/esc611:22.speaker: supporter
p2/esc611:22.text: Thanks.  Can I assist you with anything else?

p2/esc611:3.speaker: seeker
p2/esc611:3.text: my feelings fluctuate. i resent him that he ended it. it confuses me he still wants to be in my life. he said he wanted to be friends but then asked me out again. i think he is trying to work his way back in. i know i can't keep it up unless he makes it clear he wants to be with me. i don't have time for games

p2/esc611:4.speaker: supporter
p2/esc611:4.text: That does sound hard that he is giving mixed signals.

p2/esc611:5.speaker: seeker
p2/esc611:5.text: yeah i don't like that. neither does my friend. why she told him he is an idiot for letting me go

p2/esc611:6.speaker: supporter
p2/esc611:6.text: Do you think he took your friend's comments seriously?

p2/esc611:7.speaker: seeker
p2/esc611:7.text: yes cuz that's when he wanted me to be around him more

p2/esc611:8.speaker: supporter
p2/esc611:8.text: It sounds like your friend got him thinking.

p2/esc955:1.speaker: seeker
p2/esc955:1.text: I am the youngest of 5 siblings and I feel all most days now because of my parents

p2/esc955:10.speaker: seeker
p2/esc955:10.text: I do feel anxious every time.

p2/esc955:11.speaker: seeker
p2/esc955:11.text: I tried a couple of times, but my mom always sees it as being too sensitive

p2/esc955:12.speaker: supporter
p2/esc955:12.text: Sometimes it can feel impossible to talk to parents

p2/esc955:13.speaker: seeker
p2/esc955:13.text: I know, is it better if I stay away for awhile? since taking to them won't make sense?

p2/esc955:14.speaker: supporter
p2/esc955:14.text: I think that it can be very healthy to get some distance, but I think it can also feel difficult -- do you have good friends in your life that you could lean on if you needed some distance from your parents?

p2/esc955:15.speaker: seeker
p2/esc955:15.text: Yes, I do. They actually helped me coped up. I always think that I wasn't blessed with my family, but I'm blessed with good friends

p2/esc955:16.speaker: supporter
p2/esc955:16.text: Good friends can be a huge comfort and it sounds like you're a good friends yourself if you have those kinds of friendships

p2/esc955:17.speaker: seeker
p2/esc955:17.text: Thinking about it, they really did help a lot. So I should really distance myself for a while right?

p2/esc955:18.speaker: supporter
p2/esc955:18.text: I think if making distance helps you feel better, you deserve and have a right to that space

p2/esc955:19.speaker: seeker
p2/esc955:19.text: Yes, thank you. I really need to that.

p2/esc955:2.speaker: supporter
p2/esc955:2.text: It sounds like you're having a hard time feeling like you have your parents' attention, is that right?

p2/esc955:21.speaker: supporter
p2/esc955:21.text: It sounds like you are making healthy and careful emotional decisions

p2/esc955:22.speaker: supporter
p2/esc955:22.text: Is there anything else you want to discuss about your parents?

p2/esc955:3.speaker: seeker
p2/esc955:3.text: Not their attention, but more on their expectations on me

p2/esc955:5.speaker: supporter
p2/esc955:5.text: Do they do or say anything specific that makes you feel those expectations?

p2/esc955:6.speaker: seeker
p2/esc955:6.text: Yes, its more on comparing me to the children of their friends. They always say why don't I have a better job or even plans on marrying rich. Stuff like that is very frustrating

p2/esc955:7.speaker: seeker
p2/esc955:7.text: They also expect me to take care of them financially soon, I'm just starting my adult life I want to enjoy it

p2/esc955:8.speaker: supporter
p2/esc955:8.text: That sounds very frustrating. I think if I felt those kind of expectations I would be anxious.

p2/esc955:9.speaker: supporter
p2/esc955:9.text: Do you feel comfortable talking to them about your feelings?

p2/p2_conv_10:0.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_10:0.text: Hi Taylor! How have you been lately?

p2/p2_conv_10:1.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_10:1.text: Hey, I've been feeling a lot of things lately. It's been a bit overwhelming.

p2/p2_conv_10:10.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_10:10.text: That makes sense, especially with everything you have on your plate. How's your creative writing going?

p2/p2_conv_10:11.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_10:11.text: It's been up and down. I joined a writing workshop that helped, but the imposter syndrome creeps in.

p2/p2_conv_10:12.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_10:12.text: I'm glad the workshop helped. The feeling of not being enough can be so persistent. You're not alone in that.

p2/p2_conv_10:13.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_10:13.text: Thanks. It helps to know I'm not alone. The online community has been supportive too.

p2/p2_conv_10:14.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_10:14.text: That's great to hear! Sometimes finding a supportive community can make a big difference.

p2/p2_conv_10:15.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_10:15.text: Definitely! They remind me that it's okay to struggle and that growth takes time.

p2/p2_conv_10:16.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_10:16.text: Absolutely! You're on a journey, and it's perfectly okay to have ups and downs along the way.

p2/p2_conv_10:17.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_10:17.text: I truly appreciate you listening and being here for me. It means a lot.

p2/p2_conv_10:18.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_10:18.text: Anytime, Taylor. You're doing amazing things, and I'm here whenever you need to talk.

p2/p2_conv_10:19.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_10:19.text: Thank you. I'll try to take things one step at a time. Catch up soon?

p2/p2_conv_10:2.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_10:2.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what's been going on?

p2/p2_conv_10:20.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_10:20.text: Definitely! Take care and reach out whenever you feel like it.

p2/p2_conv_10:3.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_10:3.text: Yeah, I had a session with my therapist recently. We talked a lot about my self-worth.

p2/p2_conv_10:4.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_10:4.text: That sounds like an important conversation. What came up for you during the session?

p2/p2_conv_10:5.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_10:5.text: We talked about how I've been weighing my worth based on my academic and creative successes. It was eye-opening.

p2/p2_conv_10:6.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_10:6.text: It's tough when our value feels tied to achievements. How did you feel after the session?

p2/p2_conv_10:7.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_10:7.text: Honestly, I felt both relieved and a bit anxious. Relieved to recognize it but anxious about how to change it.

p2/p2_conv_10:8.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_10:8.text: Change can be challenging, but recognizing the issue is a great first step. How have things been at university?

p2/p2_conv_10:9.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_10:9.text: University's been okay. The workload is a lot, and I still struggle with feeling like I'm not doing enough.

p2/p2_conv_11:0.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_11:0.text: Hey there, is it okay to talk? I'm just feeling a bit overwhelmed with emotions right now.

p2/p2_conv_11:1.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_11:1.text: Of course, Taylor. I'm here for you. What's been going on lately?

p2/p2_conv_11:10.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_11:10.text: It feels like too much sometimes, especially after failing a mid-term recently. My self-worth is really taking a hit.

p2/p2_conv_11:11.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_11:11.text: I'm really sorry you're feeling this way, Taylor. Remember, one exam doesn't define your abilities or worth. You've achieved so much already.

p2/p2_conv_11:12.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_11:12.text: Thanks for saying that. My therapist did mention the importance of focusing on self-worth, but it’s hard to internalize it sometimes.

p2/p2_conv_11:13.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_11:13.text: It’s a process, and it’s okay to have days where it feels more challenging. Have you tried any of the strategies your therapist suggested?

p2/p2_conv_11:14.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_11:14.text: I've been trying to focus on my writing and stay active in the online community I found. It helps to some extent.

p2/p2_conv_11:15.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_11:15.text: That’s a great outlet for your emotions. Writing can be such a powerful way to process your thoughts and experiences.

p2/p2_conv_11:16.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_11:16.text: Yeah, it's one of the few things that helps me clear my mind. But the writer's block is still a bit persistent.

p2/p2_conv_11:17.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_11:17.text: Writer's block can be really frustrating, especially when you're already feeling overwhelmed. Is there anything specific about writing that's been challenging?

p2/p2_conv_11:18.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_11:18.text: It's like I'm second-guessing everything I put down on paper, feeling like it’s not good enough compared to my peers.

p2/p2_conv_11:19.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_11:19.text: Imposter syndrome is really tough to deal with. Just remember, your voice is unique and valuable in its own right.

p2/p2_conv_11:2.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_11:2.text: It's Nate, my ex. He reached out to apologize recently, and it's stirred up a lot of old memories and feelings.

p2/p2_conv_11:20.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_11:20.text: Thanks for reminding me. I often forget that when I'm deep in self-doubt. It means a lot to have your support.

p2/p2_conv_11:21.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_11:21.text: I'm always here for you, Taylor. Make sure to be kind to yourself and take things one day at a time. You're doing your best.

p2/p2_conv_11:22.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_11:22.text: Thanks. I really needed to hear that. I’ll try to focus on what's within my control and take small steps forward.

p2/p2_conv_11:23.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_11:23.text: That's a great approach. You're stronger than you realize, and I'm proud of you for reaching out and talking this through.

p2/p2_conv_11:24.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_11:24.text: I appreciate it. It feels good to get everything off my chest and know I'm not facing this alone.

p2/p2_conv_11:3.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_11:3.text: I can imagine that must be really tough. How did it feel when he reached out to you?

p2/p2_conv_11:4.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_11:4.text: Confusing, honestly. Part of me was glad he apologized, but another part isn't sure if I can trust his intentions.

p2/p2_conv_11:5.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_11:5.text: That's completely valid. Trust can be hard to rebuild, especially after everything you've been through.

p2/p2_conv_11:6.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_11:6.text: Exactly. I keep thinking about our past arguments and how they made me feel. It's all just resurfacing now.

p2/p2_conv_11:7.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_11:7.text: It sounds like those memories are really triggering some deep emotions. How are you handling them right now?

p2/p2_conv_11:8.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_11:8.text: Not too well, if I'm honest. I'm finding it hard to focus on my studies and my writing, and this time of year is already stressful.

p2/p2_conv_11:9.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_11:9.text: It's completely understandable. Between the pressure from studies and your relationship history, it sounds like you're dealing with a lot.

p2/p2_conv_12:0.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_12:0.text: Hey, are you online? I really need someone to talk to right now.

p2/p2_conv_12:1.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_12:1.text: Hey Taylor, I'm here. What's going on?

p2/p2_conv_12:10.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_12:10.text: I guess I just feel like I'm falling behind everyone else. The imposter syndrome keeps creeping in, especially when I see peers succeeding.

p2/p2_conv_12:11.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_12:11.text: Those feelings are difficult, but remember that you're not alone in experiencing them. You've achieved so much already, and you deserve to be proud of your journey.

p2/p2_conv_12:12.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_12:12.text: I know, it's just hard to see sometimes. My therapist said something about self-worth the other day, but I'm struggling to internalize it.

p2/p2_conv_12:13.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_12:13.text: That’s a common struggle. Maybe try to focus on one small thing you like or are proud of about yourself each day. It can slowly shift your perspective over time.

p2/p2_conv_12:14.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_12:14.text: That's a good idea. I’ll try to start doing that. I think just talking about it now is helping a bit.

p2/p2_conv_12:15.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_12:15.text: I'm really glad to hear that. Remember, it’s okay to have hard days. Just keep reaching out and taking things one step at a time.

p2/p2_conv_12:16.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_12:16.text: Thanks for being here. I was feeling really alone after today.

p2/p2_conv_12:17.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_12:17.text: You’re never alone in this. I’m here anytime you need to talk. We can get through this together.

p2/p2_conv_12:2.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_12:2.text: I had a panic attack today, just before a social event. It was terrifying.

p2/p2_conv_12:3.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_12:3.text: I'm so sorry to hear that. Panic attacks can be really overwhelming. Do you want to share more about what happened?

p2/p2_conv_12:4.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_12:4.text: I was supposed to go to this gathering with some classmates, and out of nowhere, I just felt completely frozen.

p2/p2_conv_12:5.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_12:5.text: That sounds incredibly tough. It makes sense you might feel that way given everything you've been dealing with lately. How are you feeling now?

p2/p2_conv_12:6.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_12:6.text: A bit better, but still shaky. I keep thinking about all the stress from before—school, my ex, even stuff at home. It all feels like too much at times.

p2/p2_conv_12:7.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_12:7.text: You’ve been through a lot recently, so it’s understandable you're feeling overwhelmed. It’s good that you’re reaching out and acknowledging what you’re experiencing.

p2/p2_conv_12:8.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_12:8.text: Thanks. I thought I was doing better with the writing workshop and finding that online community, but days like this hit hard.

p2/p2_conv_12:9.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_12:9.text: Those were really positive steps forward, and they still are. It’s okay to have setbacks. They don’t define you or erase your progress.

p2/p2_conv_13:0.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_13:0.text: Hey Taylor, how have you been feeling lately?

p2/p2_conv_13:1.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_13:1.text: Honestly, not great. I found out that my grade slipped again even after I reattempted the exam.

p2/p2_conv_13:2.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_13:2.text: I’m really sorry to hear that. I can imagine how frustrating that must be after putting in all that effort.

p2/p2_conv_13:3.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_13:3.text: Yeah, it's pretty crushing. I thought that notifying my professor and putting in the extra work would help, but apparently not.

p2/p2_conv_1:0.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_1:0.text: Hey Taylor, it's good to see you here. How are you holding up these days?

p2/p2_conv_1:1.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_1:1.text: Hey. I'm managing, I guess. Just trying to keep up with everything.

p2/p2_conv_1:10.speaker: supporter

p2/p2_conv_7:4.text: A little nervous, honestly. I feel like I should be more excited, but it’s hard with all that’s been going on.

p2/p2_conv_7:5.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_7:5.text: It's understandable to feel nervous given everything you've been dealing with. It's a lot to manage. How have things been since the argument with your ex?

p2/p2_conv_7:6.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_7:6.text: It's still a bit raw. It feels like every argument takes a bit more out of me, and it's been impacting my focus on studies too.

p2/p2_conv_7:7.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_7:7.text: That sounds exhausting. I'm really sorry you're going through this. Does being in the workshop help shift your focus a bit?

p2/p2_conv_7:8.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_7:8.text: Yes, a little. Once I'm in the zone, writing can be an escape. But starting is so daunting, especially with thoughts of the failed mid-term lingering.

p2/p2_conv_7:9.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_7:9.text: It's okay to have those feelings, Taylor. Past challenges can stick with us, but each step towards engaging with what you enjoy can help in small ways. How are you finding the support in the writing community?

p2/p2_conv_8:0.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_8:0.text: Hey Taylor! How have you been?

p2/p2_conv_8:1.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_8:1.text: Hey. I've been feeling a bit overwhelmed lately.

p2/p2_conv_8:10.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_8:10.text: It's understandable to feel that way, but remember, progress isn't always visible. You're juggling a lot, and it's okay to have setbacks.

p2/p2_conv_8:11.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_8:11.text: I guess so. Sometimes it feels like I'm not making any real progress in my writing or classes.

p2/p2_conv_8:12.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_8:12.text: Progress can be small and still meaningful. You've taken steps before, like joining that creative writing workshop. That shows dedication.

p2/p2_conv_8:13.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_8:13.text: True. The workshop was a good decision, and it helped get past my writer's block.

p2/p2_conv_8:14.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_8:14.text: Exactly, and you can overcome this too. Have you considered reaching out to someone in the workshop for support?

p2/p2_conv_8:15.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_8:15.text: Not really, but maybe I should. It might be good to connect with someone who's going through similar things.

p2/p2_conv_8:16.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_8:16.text: That sounds like a great idea! Having someone to share experiences with can really help with those feelings of imposter syndrome.

p2/p2_conv_8:17.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_8:17.text: Thanks. I think I'll do that. I appreciate you listening and helping me see other perspectives.

p2/p2_conv_8:18.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_8:18.text: Anytime, Taylor. I'm always here to listen and support you. Remember, you're not alone in this.

p2/p2_conv_8:2.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_8:2.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about it?

p2/p2_conv_8:3.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_8:3.text: Yeah... I've been struggling with imposter syndrome. It's been on my mind a lot.

p2/p2_conv_8:4.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_8:4.text: That sounds tough. What triggered these feelings for you?

p2/p2_conv_8:5.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_8:5.text: I think it started after seeing some of my peers celebrating their achievements recently. Like getting top marks or landing amazing internships.

p2/p2_conv_8:6.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_8:6.text: Seeing others succeed can definitely stir up those feelings. It's natural, but it doesn't mean you're any less capable.

p2/p2_conv_8:7.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_8:7.text: I know, but it feels like I'm going in circles. Last month was okay with finding that online community and all, but now I'm back to feeling stuck.

p2/p2_conv_8:8.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_8:8.text: I'm glad you found support in the online writing community before. Maybe leaning on them could help again? They understand the creative struggles.

p2/p2_conv_8:9.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_8:9.text: Yeah, they've been really great. It's just hard not to feel like I'm falling behind everyone else.

p2/p2_conv_9:0.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_9:0.text: Hey Taylor, how have you been lately?

p2/p2_conv_9:1.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_9:1.text: Hey. It's been a tough time, honestly. I recently saw something that's really been bothering me.

p2/p2_conv_9:10.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_9:10.text: That makes a lot of sense. Being caught in the middle can really bring up those feelings.

p2/p2_conv_9:11.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_9:11.text: And it's just been adding to everything else. Like the stress from school and my writing. It feels overwhelming.

p2/p2_conv_9:12.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_9:12.text: With everything you've been handling, it's no wonder things are feeling overwhelming. It's okay to feel that way.

p2/p2_conv_9:13.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_9:13.text: Thanks. Sometimes I feel like I'm the only one who struggles with balancing all of this.

p2/p2_conv_9:14.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_9:14.text: You're definitely not alone. Many people find themselves in similar situations and your feelings are completely valid.

p2/p2_conv_9:15.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_9:15.text: I really appreciate hearing that. I think I just need to remember that it's okay to ask for help.

p2/p2_conv_9:16.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_9:16.text: Absolutely, reaching out is a sign of strength. I'm glad you decided to talk to me about it.

p2/p2_conv_9:17.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_9:17.text: I am too. It helps knowing there's support out here. Maybe I'll eventually talk to my parents about how I feel.

p2/p2_conv_9:18.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_9:18.text: Take your time with that. Whenever you're ready, you deserve to share how you feel.

p2/p2_conv_9:19.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_9:19.text: Thanks. For now, I'll focus on the things I can control, like my writing and studies.

p2/p2_conv_9:2.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_9:2.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Would you like to talk about what happened?

p2/p2_conv_9:20.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_9:20.text: That's a great approach. Those are areas where you can certainly see progress and feel accomplished.

p2/p2_conv_9:21.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_9:21.text: Yeah, and I'm starting to feel like I can work through my writer's block. That's something positive.

p2/p2_conv_9:22.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_9:22.text: That's wonderful to hear! Remember, you're doing the best you can and that's more than enough.

p2/p2_conv_9:23.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_9:23.text: Thanks, really, for listening and helping me through this.

p2/p2_conv_9:24.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_9:24.text: Anytime, Taylor. You're doing great, and I'm here for whatever you need.

p2/p2_conv_9:3.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_9:3.text: Yeah, I guess I should. I saw my parents having a really intense argument. It's stuck with me.

p2/p2_conv_9:4.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_9:4.text: That sounds really hard to go through. Arguments like that can be really distressing to witness.

p2/p2_conv_9:5.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_9:5.text: Exactly, it's like it just hangs over me. I keep replaying it in my mind.

p2/p2_conv_9:6.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_9:6.text: It's understandable that you'd feel that way. Have you been able to talk to anyone about it?

p2/p2_conv_9:7.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_9:7.text: Not really. It's kind of hard to bring up. I don't want to make things worse between them.

p2/p2_conv_9:8.speaker: supporter
p2/p2_conv_9:8.text: I can see why you'd feel that way. Sometimes it's hard to find the right moment or words.

p2/p2_conv_9:9.speaker: seeker
p2/p2_conv_9:9.text: Yeah. It's like I don't know what's my place in it. They're my parents, but I feel like a child again.

spans.speaker: seeker
spans.exact_quote: Not too well, if I'm honest. I'm finding it hard to focus on my studies and my writing, and this time of year is already stressful.

2b07a0f5579787c984781d999af2f6d5e7754633.head: MP
2b07a0f5579787c984781d999af2f6d5e7754633.statement: experiences persistent overthinking and self-doubt regarding academic and creative work

spans.speaker: seeker
spans.exact_quote: It's like I'm second-guessing everything I put down on paper, feeling like it’s not good enough compared to my peers.

4b4089e7c0ee028fa4af220f3af384c01c0ffd74.head: MP
4b4089e7c0ee028fa4af220f3af384c01c0ffd74.statement: uses creative writing as an emotional outlet despite fluctuations in motivation and writer's block

spans.speaker: seeker
spans.exact_quote: Yeah, it's one of the few things that helps me clear my mind. But the writer's block is still a bit persistent.

spans.speaker: seeker
spans.exact_quote: It's been up and down. I joined a writing workshop that helped, but the imposter syndrome creeps in.

43b1e4ec296cf15a5544b38a6238b5acdf75ff39.statement: self-worth negatively impacted following failure on a mid-term exam

spans.speaker: seeker
spans.exact_quote: It feels like too much sometimes, especially after failing a mid-term recently. My self-worth is really taking a hit.

spans.speaker: seeker
spans.exact_quote: Yeah, and during exam week, I felt so isolated and anxious. It's been hard to shake off that feeling.

spans.exact_quote: Well, there's been a lot going on lately. I had a big argument with my ex, and my grades haven't been great either.
